summary.text: The cell membrane is a semipermeable lipid bilayer that separates and protects the interior of a cell from the outside environment.
The bilayer usually consists of phospholipids and glycolipids, and membrane proteins serve as transporters or as enzymes that help the cell interact with its environment.
It controls the movement of substances in and out of a cell and takes part in processes such as cell adhesion and cell signaling.

facts.label: Lipid idea
facts.value: Ernest Overton proposed membranes were made of lipids in 1895

facts.label: Bilayer hypothesis
facts.value: Proposed by Gorter and Grendel in 1925

facts.label: Fluid mosaic model
facts.value: Singer and Nicolson, 1972; still the main picture

facts.label: Red blood cell test
facts.value: Extracted lipid covered about twice the cells' surface area

items.prompt: Gorter and Grendel extracted lipid from mature mammalian red blood cells to study the membrane. Why were those cells a clever choice?

options.label: They have no nuclei or organelles, so the plasma membrane is their only lipid-containing structure
They have the thickest membranes of any cell, which are easiest to measure
They contain no proteins, so their membranes are pure lipid
They are the largest cells, so they give the most lipid to work with

items.explain: Mature mammalian red blood cells lack a nucleus and organelles, so all the extracted lipid could be assumed to come from the plasma membrane.

items.prompt: The extracted lipid covered roughly double the surface area calculated for the cells it came from. What did the researchers conclude about the membrane?

options.label: It has a single layer of lipid with protein on top
It is made mostly of protein, with little lipid
It is thinner than any single molecule could be
It has two layers of lipid, a bilayer

items.explain: The roughly 2:1 area ratio led them to conclude the plasma membrane contains a lipid bilayer.

items.prompt: In the late 1800s scientists argued over whether cell membranes existed at all. What was a main reason?

options.label: Only plant cells had been observed, and plants have no membrane
Membranes dissolve whenever cells are stained for viewing
Microscopes were not yet good enough to tell membranes from cell walls
Everyone agreed membranes were vital, so nobody tested the idea

items.explain: By the second half of the 19th century, microscopy still could not distinguish cell membranes from cell walls, and many refuted the membrane's existence.

items.prompt: A 1930s model pictured the membrane as a lipid bilayer sandwiched between thin layers of another substance. What was that substance?

options.label: Cholesterol
Protein
Cellulose
Water

items.explain: The paucimolecular model suggested a lipid bilayer lay between two thin protein layers.

items.prompt: A cell lets certain ions and organic molecules cross its boundary but keeps others out. Which property of the membrane allows this?

options.label: It is a rigid wall that nothing can cross
It is selectively permeable
It is fully open, so only concentration decides
It is welded shut by peripheral proteins

items.explain: The cell membrane controls what moves in and out and is selectively permeable to ions and organic molecules.

items.prompt: Which molecule, placed between the lipids of an animal cell's membrane, helps keep it suitably fluid across temperatures?

options.label: Glycolipid, which hardens the membrane at every temperature
Cellulose, which gives the membrane a firm frame
Cholesterol, a sterol
Peripheral protein, which melts the lipids apart

items.explain: Eukaryotes typically have sterols such as cholesterol (in animals) between the lipids, maintaining appropriate membrane fluidity at various temperatures.
